name: Herod Agrippa II
bio: King Agrippa (Herod Agrippa II), son of Herod Agrippa I, came with his sister Bernice to Caesarea to greet the new governor Festus; when Festus explained Paul's case, Agrippa asked to hear Paul himself, and the next day, with great pomp, he and Bernice entered the hall to hear Paul's defense (Acts 25:13-27). He is a different figure from his father, Herod Agrippa I, who had earlier persecuted the church and imprisoned Peter. His further role in questioning Paul is told in the chapters ahead. Agrippa gave Paul leave to speak in his own defense and listened as Paul recounted his conversion and ministry; when Paul appealed directly to his belief in the prophets, Agrippa admitted he was almost persuaded to become a Christian. He concluded privately with Festus and Bernice that Paul had done nothing worthy of death, remarking that Paul could have been released had he not appealed to Caesar (Acts 26:1-32).
